cardTitle: How long do two classes read?

fixIts.flawed: Don't you think reading is great?
fixIts.fix: How many minutes did you read yesterday?
How many books did you read this month?

planPrompt: 🤔 Make a guess! How many minutes did most kids read?

graphLab.tell: 📊 What do the two graphs tell us?
graphLab.notTell: 🤔 What can't these graphs tell us?
tellAnswers: Class A's answers are close together, from {min} to {max}.
Class B's answers are spread out, from {minB} to {maxB}.
Both classes have a mean of {meanA} minutes.
notTellAnswers: They don't tell us why one class reads differently.
They don't tell us what the kids read.
They don't tell us how fast the kids read.

chanceLab.story: 📖 Pip uses chance to pick the next class book!

evidenceBoard.claimPrompt: 👀 Look at your findings. How are Class A and Class B different?
claimAnswers: Class B's answers are more spread out
Class A's answers are closer together
both classes have the same mean
becauseAnswers: Class B's range is {rangeB}, and Class A's is {rangeA}
the mean of both classes is {meanA} minutes

reasonAnswers: the mean of both classes is {meanA} minutes
Class B has a range of {rangeB}
the data showed me something new
numberLab.predictPrompt: 🤔 Guess first! If every kid read the same, how many minutes would that be?
numberLab.build: 📖 5 kids read some minutes. Their mean is {target}. Type 5 numbers that fit.

mistake.story: 📖 Mia asked 5 friends how long they read.

compareRange.story: 📖 Both classes have the same mean. Now look at the range.
compareRange.question: Which class's answers are more spread out?
